newsitem.title: USA: GM names new heads of Cadillac, Buick.
newsitem.headline: GM names new heads of Cadillac, Buick.

text.p: General Motors Corp on Wednesday replaced the long-time heads of its Buick and Cadillac divisions, two car lines that have been plagued by slow sales in recent years.

Robert Coletta, 59, who had been general sales and service manager of Buick, was named GM vice president and general manager of the division, succeeding Edward Mertz, 59, who is retiring after 40 years with GM. Mertz had been head of Buick since 1986. At Cadillac, John F. Smith, 45, replaces John Grettenberger, 59, as general manager, a post Grettenberger had held since 1984.
Grettenberger will retire after 34 years with GM.
Smith was previously president of GM's Allison Transmission Division. His old job will be filled by Daniel Hancock, 46, who had been director of transmission engineering at GM Powertrain Group.

The appointments and retirements will be effective February 1, 1997. The changes mean GM has replaced the top managers at four of its seven vehicle divisions since Ronald Zarrella joined as the automaker's marketing chief in December 1994.
Coletta and Smith will both report to Zarrella.

A native of Memphis, Tenn., Coletta joined GM in 1955 as a Buick service representative in the Memphis zone, and earned a bachelor's degree in business administration from General Motors Institute in 1960.

He worked his way up through the Buick sales and service organization, becoming assistant general sales manager for the midwest and later northeast areas. Coletta had been general manager of sales and service for Buick since 1987.
Smith had been president of Indianapolis-based Allison Transmission since December 1994. Before that, he was stationed in Zurich as a GM-Europe vice president of planning.

Smith has held several management positions within the GM financial staff in Detroit and its Treasurer's Office in New York City. A native of Kansas City, Mo., Smith has a bachelor's degree in engineering from General Motors Institute and an MBA from Harvard University.
